records.notes: Civil Appeal No. 709 of 1962 before the Supreme Court of India. Tenant challenged landlord's decree for ejectment/eviction under Bombay Rent Act, arguing that inherent powers under Section 151 CPC override summary suit procedure under Order 37. Supreme Court held inherent powers cannot be exercised to circumvent express statutory provisions, held summary decree valid, and dismissed appeal with costs. Successful party is respondent under Section 5 Row 124 of guidelines.
records.case_title: Civil Appeal No. 709 of 1962 of RAMKARANDAS RADHAVALLABH Vs BHAGWANDAS DWARKADAS
records.disposition_rationale: Supreme Court held that Rule 8 of Bombay High Court Original Side Rules and Section 151 CPC do not permit the court to circumvent procedural statutory bars, affirming the eviction decree on the merits.
records.party_success_rationale: Respondent landlord Bhagwandas Dwarkadas successfully defeated tenant's legal challenge and maintained the decree for eviction with costs awarded by the Supreme Court.

records.notes: Civil Writ Petition under Article 226 (W.P.(C) 4189/2016) by Head Constable Brijesh Kumar Shukla challenging arbitrary Movement order transferring him to 140 Battalion without medical facilities needed for his mentally retarded, spastic son. High Court recorded respondent's concession regarding vacancy and medical facilities at 32 Battalion Hissar, quashed the impugned transfer order, and directed fresh posting to Hissar. Petitioner obtained full substantive relief prayed for; successful party is petitioner under Section 5 Row 124 of guidelines.
